title: openai-compat: normalize tool_choice semantics and tool message formatting, add schema mapping improvements
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: downstream customers rely on OpenAI-compatible semantics for tool/function calling. We found two sources of user-facing mismatch: 1) tool_choice behavior was underspecified and returned inconsistent metadata for multi-tool responses, confusing fe-be routing; 2) tool messages were emitted with internal framing (stringified JSON blobs and inconsistent 'name' vs 'tool' fields), which broke strict OpenAI schema validators and caused SDKs to mis-handle tool outputs. This PR standardizes tool_choice semantics, introduces a deterministic tool selection payload, maps internal tool schemas to OpenAI-style 'arguments' schemas where possible, and normalizes message formatting for tool outputs. Changes include: - Define canonical tool_choice object schema and populate 'tool_choice' top-level field in assistant responses when a tool is selected. - Add mapping layer that converts internal tool interface definitions to OpenAI-compatible JSON Schema (title/description/type/properties/required) to improve compatibility with schema-aware clients. - Normalize tool messages to include: role: "tool", name: <tool_name>, content: <stringified-result-or-structured-json>, content_type: "application/json" when data is structured. - Preserve legacy fallbacks (legacy_tool_payload) for customers on older SDK versions for two release cycles. - Tests: unit tests for schema mapper, integration tests covering streaming with tool invocation and a fixture asserting tool_choice stability under concurrent requests. Checklist: - [x] Spec: add canonical tool_choice docs and examples - [x] Implementation: server-side mapping + message formatter - [x] SDK compatibility checks (Python/TS) - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Changelog/release notes

merge_commit_message:
openai-compat: standardize tool_choice semantics, schema mapping and tool message formatting

Closes ENG-3421. Adds schema mapper, message normalizer, legacy fallback and tests.
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: tool/function calling: The compat layer now emits a canonical 'tool_choice' object in assistant responses and normalizes tool messages to include role/name/content/content_type. Internal tool definitions are mapped to OpenAI-style JSON Schema when possible. Legacy fallback retained for two release cycles. Developers should update SDKs to read response.tool_choice and not rely on ad-hoc parsing of tool messages.
notes_for_backport: No backport to stable-1.3 required. Recommend cherry-pick to release/1.4 if customers request earlier compat behavior. Backport must include schema mapper and formatter changes and updated SDK shims.
pr_body_plain: See description field. The PR focuses on compatibility invariants: canonical tool_choice, JSON Schema mapping for tools, and structured tool message formatting. Tests and docs included.
user_visible_changes: Responses now include response.tool_choice when a tool is chosen (stable field)
Tool messages use content_type: application/json for structured outputs
SDKs should use response.tool_choice to decide routing/handlers instead of scanning messages
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: breaking older SDKs that inspected messages in a non-deterministic way. Mitigation: legacy_tool_payload included for two release cycles, and SDKs have been updated in tandem with deprecation warnings in CHANGELOG.
how_to_verify: 1) Run integration/tool_streaming_invoke.yaml to exercise streaming tool invocations. 2) Use sdk/python example to call an agent that triggers a tool; assert response.tool_choice is present and tool message content_type is application/json. 3) Run unit tests: go test ./compat -bench=.
related_links: Issue SUP-879: customer reported invalid schema on tool outputs
auditors: SRE: load test pass at 10k req/s with feature flag enabled
post_merge_tasks: Publish compat docs update to docs site
Increment SDK compat version and release minor SDK updates
Monitor errors for 48h for increased parsing failures
internal_notes: We intentionally do not attempt to perfectly map every complex internal tool interface to JSON Schema; we provide best-effort mapping and an 'opaque' fallback that is documented. Future follow-ups: add richer examples for nested arrays/union types (ENG-3502).
